purpose: Replace the break-even projection's assumed fixed-cost share with a measured per-segment breakdown on the TP1 arm, and record the host-side term the projection omits.

protocol.note: the harness reads back every token, so its window per step includes a sampler readback the tok/s protocol amortizes; kernel-family times are device time and are unaffected

findings: The family-duration sums are not a critical path. Summed kernel durations exceed the measured window on the W7900 (about 30 ms of family totals plus 19.2 ms of interior gap inside a 34.9 ms window) because dispatch intervals on this route overlap - the harness reports a dispatch overlap ratio of 1.916 and warns that per-family shares are shares of kernel time, not of the device union. Dividing those sums by a different protocol's token time therefore does not establish a fixed-cost share, and no fixed-share range is narrowed by this artifact.

The measured kernel-family times are still useful as a device-time profile of the step: weight reads dominate (25.95 ms/step on the W7900, 21.77 on the XTX), attention + GDN + sampler + copy are small next to them (1.578 and 1.441 ms/step), and the two cards' 1.19x weight-read ratio matches their 1.20x TP1 token-rate ratio. That is a statement about where device time goes, not about what a TP2 group's critical path would be.

The projection's fixed-cost term is broader than non-matmul kernels: it stands for attention, GDN recurrence, and launch and scheduling overhead, which does not shrink with tensor parallelism. Launch and scheduling cost is exactly what the family table does not measure. The 20% and 30% rows therefore stay as sensitivity cases until measured segment walls replace the assumption, and the 0% and 10% rows are equally unconfirmed by this artifact.

Each decode step issues ~811 kernel launches. That is the per-rank structural term a TP2 group would have to carry on both ranks, and it is the reason a shard's saving cannot be read off a family-duration table.

The harness's window also contains a per-token sampler readback (about 9 ms/step of hipMemcpy API time) that the tok/s protocol amortizes, so its interior-gap split is not the tok/s protocol's. It is recorded as a candidate missing term rather than as the projection's host cost: 19.2 ms (W7900) and 22.6 ms (XTX) of interior gap per step, of which 15.3 and 16.2 ms has no HIP API in flight.

sources.w7900: rocprofv3 kernel/marker/HIP/memory-copy trace of the R0 resident session, 512 prompt rows, 128 decode tokens, HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0

limitations: Kernel-family attribution is device time from a rocprofv3 trace of the R0 resident session. Dispatch intervals overlap, so family durations are not additive and not a critical path. It is not a shard-shaped segment measurement: no shard-shaped weight layout exists in the engine, so the sharded MLP/attention/GDN segment times the decision rule needs are still unmeasured.

The interior-gap split is specific to this harness, which reads back every token; the tok/s protocol amortizes that readback. Gap numbers are indicative of the launch structure, not exact for the tok/s protocol.
No compute -> exchange -> compute sequence has been measured.
Both cards are gfx1100 and were measured in the same session with the same protocol, so the two columns are comparable to each other.
next_measurements: A shard-shaped MLP segment: build a half-intermediate Q4_K weight layout and time the engine's own GEMV dispatch on it, on both cards, so the compute saving is measured rather than assumed.
Replicated versus single-owner attention and GDN segment times at full and half head counts.
Representative compute -> exchange -> compute sequences using the native transport, at the measured per-reduction cost.
A launch-gap measurement on the tok/s protocol path, so the projection's omitted host term is bounded.
does_not_establish: a fixed-cost share, or any narrowing of the projection's 0-30% sensitivity range
a critical path for the TP1 step: the family sums overlap and are not additive
a shard-shaped segment time, which needs a rank-local weight layout
